<Aside type="danger" title="Superseded — describes the retired papercuspai.com marketplace">
This page documents the standalone **`papercuspai.com` marketplace**
(`Papercusp/papercusp-registry`, Cloudflare Pages + Tunnel + a Hono
`marketplace-api` on `:3057`) as of the 2026-04-27 handoff. That public
marketplace surface is **no longer the current distribution path.**

What replaced it: the in-app **Cupboard** — a GitHub-backed listing service
served by `apps/operator-public` (Cloudflare Workers + Hono + D1), with the
desktop operator owning the listing UI. Listings span six kinds
(`harness | blueprint | plugin | pack | knowledge-pack | template`); the
runtime-less code-tool pack is `pack` (briefly `tool-pack` under migration 008,
since renamed back — the `tool-pack` value still parses as an alias), and the
`snapshot` kind was retired (Cupboard migration 008 drops it from the
`listing_kind` CHECK constraint — see `retire-snapshots-instance-spec-2026-06-09`). Publish/install
flow through the
`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/cupboard.ts` operator routes
and the `apps/papercusp-publish` Worker, with agent verbs `blueprint:*`
(`catalog`/`create`/`extend`/`validate`/`publish`). There is no `snapshots:*`
verb — the reproducible clone is the lightweight InstanceSpec, not a published
snapshot.
Read the rest of this page as a historical record of the earlier design, not
the current system.
</Aside>

The marketplace is the public-facing component of Papercusp described in [§11 Distribution](/internal/docs/spec/distribution). This page tracks what's actually shipped vs. what's still spec'd-only.

## Two surfaces, often confused

There are **two distinct user-facing apps** in this project, both legitimate, both needed. They serve different audiences:

| Surface | URL | Source | Audience | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Substrate operator dashboard** | http://localhost:3055 | `libs/papercusp/apps/web/` (in [Papercusp/papercusp](https://github.com/Papercusp/papercusp) submodule) | Anyone running their own Papercusp install | Manage local API keys, browse the catalog with installed-state, view harness state, sign in for publishing |
| **Public marketplace** | https://papercuspai.com | `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site/` (in [Papercusp/papercusp-registry](https://github.com/Papercusp/papercusp-registry) submodule) | Anyone on the internet discovering Papercusp | Browse the catalog read-only, read docs, see featured packages, get install instructions |

### Why both exist (not a duplicate, not a stale-link mistake)

- The substrate operator UI is **part of every Papercusp install** — anyone self-hosting gets it. Its `/marketplace` page hits a LOCAL `/api/marketplace/catalog` route, which proxies to `api.papercuspai.com/catalog` and adds local install state ("you have this installed", "newer version available", etc.). That's only meaningful if you have an install.

- The public marketplace at papercuspai.com is **install-free** — it just shows the catalog. No login, no install state, no API keys. Anyone evaluating Papercusp lands here first.

The substrate UI and public site share the same data source (`api.papercuspai.com`) but render different concerns. **Not a stale duplicate.**

## Architecture (current state)

```
papercuspai.com  (Cloudflare Pages — static Next.js export)
   │
   │ runtime fetch (CORS-allowed origin)
   ▼
api.papercuspai.com  (Cloudflare Tunnel — public ingress)
   │
   │ tunnel → cloudflared (token mode)
   │   tunnel UUID c53515b3-edfe-4e99-813b-e3916ae9d02c (papercupai-api)
   ▼
http://localhost:3057  (marketplace-api — Hono on Node)
   │   ../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/
   │
   │ filesystem read
   ▼
~/.papercusp/marketplace-storage/<slug>/<version>/
   ├── papercusp.json          (manifest)
   ├── README.md               (rendered on detail page)
   └── <slug>-<version>.tar.gz (the install)
```

### Endpoints implemented in marketplace-api

```typescript
GET    /healthz                          → "ok"
GET    /catalog                          → { catalog: [{...manifest, versions[]}], storageRoot }
GET    /catalog/:slug                    → { slug, versions, latest: manifest }
GET    /catalog/:slug/:version           → { slug, version, manifest, readme }
GET    /download/:slug/:version          → tarball stream (application/gzip)
POST   /publish/:slug/:version           → multipart upload (manifest + tarball + readme)
DELETE /catalog/:slug/:version           → unpublish (dev-only)
```

POST `/publish` is currently in **open** mode (no auth). It supports a PAT-auth mode via `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_AUTH=pat` that verifies the Authorization header against the GitHub user API and records the verified login as `publishedBy`.

### Marketplace site features

- **Landing page** (`/`) — live-fetches 3 featured packages from `/catalog`; "How it works" section; "Publish your own harness" CTA with sample command.
- **Catalog grid** (`/marketplace/`) — live fetch + client-side search by name/description/author. Cards show name, version, author, description, role count, plugin count.
- **Package detail** (`/marketplace/[slug]/`) — manifest + rendered README; install command with copy button; download tarball link; sidebar listing roles (with preferred models), plugins, schema files, version history, substrate compat range.
- **Docs** (`/docs/`) — quickstart placeholder with CLI install/run commands. Full reference link to spec site.

## Implementation plan — by spec section

For each spec'd feature in §11, this is the planned implementation route. Items are ordered by priority (auth → reliability → UX → discovery → governance).

### Phase M1 — Auth on publish (§11.6)

**Goal:** Anyone publishing under `@user/foo` must prove ownership of GitHub user `user`.

**Plan:**

1. Add GitHub OAuth app at `github.com/Papercusp` (or repurpose existing). Redirect URI: `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/auth/github/callback`.
2. Add session middleware to marketplace-api (signed cookies; HMAC key from env).
3. New endpoints:
   - `GET /v1/auth/github/login` → redirect to GitHub authorize URL
   - `GET /v1/auth/github/callback` → exchange code, verify token, set session cookie
   - `GET /v1/auth/me` → return verified GitHub identity
   - `POST /v1/auth/logout` → clear cookie
4. Modify `POST /publish/:slug/:version`:
   - Reject if no session cookie OR session's GitHub login doesn't match the `@owner` namespace prefix in `:slug`.
   - Stamp manifest with `publishedBy: <github-login>` server-side.
5. CLI `papercusp publish` — open browser to `/v1/auth/github/login`, capture session cookie, persist to `~/.papercusp/credentials.json` (mode 0600).
6. Rejection messages must be specific: `"foo/bar" requires GitHub user "foo"; you're authenticated as "baz"`.

**Estimate:** 3-4 hours work. CSRF protection, scope validation, retry-on-token-expiry are the hard parts.

### Phase M2 — R2 storage backing ✅ CODE SHIPPED (gated, awaiting credentials)

**Status:** All code paths shipped. Activates the moment R2 credentials are added to the env. **No code changes needed when the user has the bucket + token.**

**What shipped:**

- New module `apps/marketplace-api/src/r2.ts` — S3-SDK against R2 endpoint; `isR2Configured()`/`putFile`/`putBytes`/`presign`/`exists`/`deleteKey`. Lazy client init, throws clearly if env missing.
- Schema delta `sql/006-r2-backing.sql` — adds `r2_key`, `r2_signature_key`, `r2_uploaded_at` columns to `package_versions` (idempotent).
- `POST /publish/:slug/:version` — after the FS write, also uploads tarball + `signature.json` to R2 (best-effort, non-fatal). Records `r2_key` in DB. Response now includes `r2: { key }` or `r2: { configured: false }`.
- `GET /download/:slug/:version` — when R2 is configured AND the version has been uploaded there, redirects to a 60s presigned URL (or to `R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL/<key>` when set). Falls back to FS streaming otherwise.
- New endpoint `GET /v1/storage/status` — returns `{ configured, account?, bucket?, publicBaseUrl? }` for ops visibility.
- New endpoint `POST /v1/storage/backfill-r2` — operator-token-gated; uploads up to 100 unbackfilled versions per call. Idempotent (skips versions with `r2_key` already set).
- npm deps added: `@aws-sdk/client-s3`, `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`.

**To activate:**

1. Create R2 bucket in Cloudflare dashboard (account `f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94`)
2. Generate an R2 API token (R2 → Manage API Tokens → "Object Read & Write" on the bucket)
3. Append to `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env`:
   ```
   R2_ACCOUNT_ID=f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94
   R2_BUCKET=papercusp-marketplace-tarballs
   R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<from token>
   R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<from token>
   # Optional: R2_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://r2.papercuspai.com (if you set up a public bucket / CDN)
   ```
4. `bin/overmind-all restart marketplace`
5. Verify: `curl localhost:3057/v1/storage/status` → `"configured": true`
6. Backfill existing tarballs: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_OPERATOR_TOKEN" localhost:3057/v1/storage/backfill-r2`

After backfill, all downloads transparently 302-redirect to R2. Future publishes dual-write FS + R2.

**Verified:** marketplace-api boots cleanly in disabled mode (`[r2] disabled — set ...`); `/v1/storage/status` returns `{"configured":false}`; `/download/...` still serves from FS. No regressions.

### Phase M2.5 — Postgres metadata table

**Goal:** Replace `listSlugs` / `listVersions` filesystem walks with a Postgres-backed catalog.

**Schema** (in `papercusp_marketplace` schema):

```sql
CREATE TABLE packages (
  slug          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- @owner/package
  owner         TEXT NOT NULL,            -- verified GitHub login
  description   TEXT,
  homepage      TEXT,
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  retracted     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active'  -- 'active' | 'deprecated' | 'withdrawn' | 'quarantined'
);

CREATE TABLE package_versions (
  slug              TEXT REFERENCES packages(slug),
  version           TEXT NOT NULL,
  manifest_json     JSONB NOT NULL,
  readme_md         TEXT,
  install_shape     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'iterative' | 'scheduled' | 'reactive' | 'passive'
  capability_tiers  JSONB,                  -- { low: N, medium: N, high: N } counts
  service_pins      JSONB,                  -- { tasks: '^1.0', secrets: '^2.0', ... }
  signature         TEXT NOT NULL,          -- Ed25519 base64
  tarball_size      BIGINT NOT NULL,
  tarball_sha256    TEXT NOT NULL,
  tarball_r2_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
  published_by      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- GitHub login
  published_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  yanked_at         TIMESTAMPTZ,
  yanked_reason     TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (slug, version)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_package_versions_published_at ON package_versions(published_at DESC);
```

**Estimate:** 1 hour for schema + 1 hour migrating reads. Bundle with M2.

### Phase M3 — Tarball signing (Ed25519)

**Goal:** Detect tampering between publish and install.

**Plan:**

1. Generate marketplace's Ed25519 keypair; private key stored at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-key.pem` on the marketplace-api host (mode 0600); public key published at `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/keys/marketplace.pub`.
2. At publish:
   - Compute SHA-256 of the tarball.
   - Sign `${slug}\n${version}\n${sha256}\n${published_by}\n${published_at}` with the marketplace key.
   - Store the signature in `package_versions.signature`.
3. At install:
   - CLI fetches the marketplace public key (cached locally with TTL of 1 day).
   - Verifies signature against the metadata it received from `/catalog/:slug/:version`.
   - Independently SHA-256 the downloaded tarball and verify it matches the signed sha256.
4. Failure modes:
   - Signature invalid → install hard-fails with "tarball tampered or marketplace key changed".
   - Public key fetched but doesn't match cached → CLI prompts user to confirm rotation (single line, audit logged).

**Estimate:** 2 hours. The crypto is `tweetnacl`-grade primitives.

### Phase M4 — Search + tags (Typesense) ✅ SHIPPED real fuzzy search

**Status:** Live with Typesense backend; falls back gracefully to LIKE-based SQL when Typesense is unavailable.

**What shipped:**

- New module `apps/marketplace-api/src/typesense.ts` — collection schema, `indexPackage` / `unindexPackage` / `searchTypesense`
- `marketplace_packages` collection (slug, description, owner, latest_version, capabilities[], plugins[], shape, retracted, downloads_30d, updated_at)
- `/v1/search?q=…&shape=…` hits Typesense first with fuzzy matching (2-typo tolerance + prefix), falls back to SQL LIKE on failure
- `&shape=` filter facet (iterative / scheduled / reactive / passive)
- Response includes `backend: 'typesense' | 'sql'` so callers know which path served them
- Sync hooks: every `POST /publish/...` upserts the doc; every `withdraw`/`quarantine` removes it; `unwithdraw`/`unquarantine`/(un)`deprecate` re-syncs the retracted state
- Operator endpoint `POST /v1/admin/reindex-typesense` — bulk re-index existing packages (idempotent)

**Verified:** typo `codign` correctly resolves to `papercup-coding` ("Did you mean?" semantics for free); responses through tunnel show `backend: 'typesense'`.

### Phase M5 — Update / uninstall flows (§11.7, §11.8)

**Goal:** `papercusp update <name>` and `papercusp uninstall <name>` work per spec.

**Plan:**

1. Substrate-side state: `installed_plugins` table tracking `{ slug, version, applied_migration_index, granted_capabilities, install_path, installed_at }`.
2. CLI `papercusp update <slug>` flow per [§11.7](/spec/distribution/#117-update-flow):
   - Fetch latest version from marketplace
   - Diff capabilities (added/removed/renamed/major)
   - Prompt only for additions (unless major version → re-prompt all)
   - Snapshot old version to `~/.papercusp/installed/<slug>/.snapshots/<old-version>/` (manifest + schema dump + granted-caps)
   - Apply new migrations from `applied_migration_index`
   - Reconcile routines (delete renamed, insert new, update existing in-place)
   - Replace plugin code on disk
3. CLI `papercusp uninstall <slug>` flow per [§11.8](/spec/distribution/#118-uninstall-flow):
   - Default: stop code, leave data
   - `--purge-data`: also drop plugin schema
4. CLI `papercusp rollback <slug>`: re-mount snapshot version (DB rollback is user's responsibility — substrate doesn't run down-migrations).

**Estimate:** 5-6 hours. The capability-diff logic is the hard part; everything else is filesystem + Postgres mechanics.

### Phase M6 — Retraction (§11.9)

**Goal:** Server-side package status — Deprecated / Yanked / Withdrawn / Quarantined.

**Plan:**

1. Add `retracted` column to `packages` (already in M2.5 schema).
2. Add `yanked_at` / `yanked_reason` to `package_versions` (already in M2.5 schema).
3. New endpoints:
   - `POST /v1/packages/:slug/deprecate` (owner-only)
   - `POST /v1/packages/:slug/withdraw` (owner OR operator)
   - `POST /v1/packages/:slug/quarantine` (operator-only)
   - `POST /v1/packages/:slug/versions/:version/yank` (owner OR operator)
4. Marketplace-api list endpoints (`/catalog`, `/v1/search`) filter by `retracted` status:
   - `deprecated` → still returned with a flag in the response
   - `yanked` versions → hidden from listings
   - `withdrawn` packages → hidden from listings
   - `quarantined` packages → hidden + tarball returns 410 immediately
5. Substrate periodically polls `/v1/installed-status?slugs=A,B,C&versions=...` (every hour) to detect retractions of installed plugins. On `quarantined`, auto-pause routines from that plugin and surface UI alert.
6. Public audit log at `papercuspai.com/security/quarantines` (page generated at build, sourced from `/v1/admin/quarantine-log`).

**Estimate:** 3-4 hours including the polling client in the substrate.

### Phase M7 — Detail page rich UX

**Goal:** Detail page surfaces install shape, service pins, capability tiers (already mentioned in §11.4).

**Plan:**

1. Update `/marketplace/[slug]/page.tsx` to read these fields from `manifest`:
   - `manifest.shape` (from §4.1) — render as a colored badge
   - `manifest.services` (from §8.4.1) — render as a list with version ranges
   - `manifest.capabilities` — bucket by tier (§10.6.1) and show "low: N · medium: N · high: N" with a warning icon if high > 0
2. Add a "Trust" badge:
   - ✅ Verified (signed + verified GitHub identity)
   - ⚠ Unverified (valid namespace, no signature)
3. Add a "Last updated" date and version count.
4. Show `publishedBy` (GitHub login with link to user profile).

**Estimate:** 2-3 hours. Pure UI; data is already in the manifest once M1 + M3 land.

### Marketplace operator dashboard ✅ SHIPPED

**Status:** Live at `http://localhost:3001/papercusp-marketplace-ops` (internal reference app admin).

**What shipped:**

- Marketplace API endpoint `GET /v1/admin/overview` (operator-token-gated) — returns aggregate health: package counts by state, authors, reviews, downloads-today, SBOM scan backlog, vulnerability severity histogram, webhook subscription health, R2 status, recent publishes (10), recent retractions (10).
- Admin route `/papercusp-marketplace-ops` (internal reference app admin) — server-renders the dashboard reading the operator token from `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env` (token never reaches browser).
- API proxy at `/api/marketplace-ops-overview` — used for the 30s client-side polling.

4. Site uses `popularity` field (last 30 days' downloads) to:

   - Compute a "Trending this week" section (biggest week-over-week % gainers).

### Phase M10 — Size & bandwidth quotas (§11.10)

**Goal:** Enforce the per-package, per-publisher, per-IP limits to prevent abuse.

**Plan:**

1. **Per-package limits at upload:**
   - Reject `POST /publish` early if `Content-Length` > 50 MB.
   - Validate manifest size ≤ 64 KB before parse.
   - Validate README size ≤ 256 KB after extraction.
2. **Per-publisher quotas** — table `publisher_quotas { github_login, day, publishes_count, total_bytes }`:
   - 50 publishes/day check at upload time.
   - Aggregate-storage check by summing `package_versions.tarball_size` for all of the publisher's packages.
3. **Per-IP throttling** — middleware on the marketplace-api Hono router:
   - In-memory `Map<ip, { count, windowStart }>` with 1-minute windows for read endpoints.
   - For `/download/`, hourly windows.
   - For `/publish/`, per-authenticated-user windows (not IP).
   - Returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header.
4. **Cloudflare-side rate limit rules** for the `api.papercuspai.com` zone. Currently no token scope to configure these via API; must be added via CF dashboard.

**Estimate:** 3-4 hours (most of it is plumbing the in-memory rate limiter and the publisher-quota table).

### Phase M11 — Catalog webhooks (§11.11)

**Goal:** CI / mirrors / external monitors get notified on catalog events.

**Plan:**

1. Schema:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE webhook_subscriptions (
     id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
     owner           TEXT NOT NULL,           -- '@owner' or '*' (operator only)
     url             TEXT NOT NULL,
     events          TEXT[] NOT NULL,         -- ['version.published', ...]
     secret          TEXT NOT NULL,           -- HMAC key
     created_by      TEXT NOT NULL,           -- GitHub login that registered it
     created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
     last_delivery   TIMESTAMPTZ,             -- updated on success
     consecutive_fails INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
     disabled_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
   );

   CREATE TABLE webhook_deliveries (
     id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- 'wh_evt_01J6...' (event id)
     subscription_id TEXT REFERENCES webhook_subscriptions(id),
     event           TEXT NOT NULL,
     ts              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
     payload         JSONB NOT NULL,
     attempt         INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
     status_code     INT,
     completed_at    TIMESTAMPTZ
   );
   ```
2. Endpoints:
   - `POST /v1/webhooks` — register subscription; auth-gated (only namespace owner can subscribe to events for that namespace).
   - `DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id` — owner-only.
   - `GET /v1/webhooks` — list subscriber's webhooks + delivery history (last 100 attempts each).
3. Producer side: `version.published`, `version.yanked`, `package.withdrawn`, `package.quarantined` events insert into `webhook_deliveries` with attempt=0 within the publish/retract transaction.
4. Worker process: long-lived loop polls `webhook_deliveries` where `completed_at IS NULL`, dispatches with HMAC-SHA-256 signature header, retries per spec schedule. Could run inside marketplace-api or as separate microservice; start in marketplace-api.
5. After 90 days of failed delivery, mark subscription `disabled_at`. Send one warning email (via Resend or similar) before disable.

**Estimate:** 4-5 hours. The worker loop is the hard part — must be exactly-once enough that owners can dedup confidently.

### Phase M12 — Vendored / offline install (§11.12)

**Goal:** `papercusp pack` produces a self-contained mirror; substrate can install from `file://` URL.

**Plan:**

1. **CLI command** `papercusp pack <slug>[@<version>] [<slug2>]... --output <dir>`:
   - Authenticates against the configured registry.
   - For each requested package, downloads the tarball + manifest + README.
   - If signed (per §11.5/M3), bundles the signature file too.
   - Bundles the marketplace's public verification key.
   - Writes a `marketplace-snapshot.json` with the catalog state as of pack time (lets the offline substrate respond to "what versions exist?" queries).
   - Writes `index.json` per package (the "latest" pointer + version list).
2. **Substrate resolver changes** in `@papercusp/cli`:
   - `papercusp config set registry file:///path/to/dir/` accepted.
   - Loader uses `node:fs/promises` for `file://` URLs; same JSON shapes as HTTP.
   - Signature verification works identically (the public key is bundled).
3. **Refresh tooling**:
   - `papercusp pack --refresh <existing-mirror-dir>` — re-fetches all packages currently in the mirror, updating to latest.
   - `papercusp pack --diff <existing-mirror-dir> <other-dir>` — show what changed between two pack snapshots.

**Estimate:** 5-6 hours. The `file://` resolver + bundled public key are the new mechanics; rest is filesystem walks.

### Phase M13 — Multi-registry resolution (§11.13)

**Goal:** Support scope-based registry routing, no automatic fallback.

**Plan:**

1. CLI parses `~/.papercusp/config.json` for `registries[]`.
2. For each install/update/lookup request, walk the list:
   - Find the first registry whose `scope` matches the requested package.
   - Issue the request to ONLY that registry.
   - On failure: if `trustOnFail` is `false` (default), return error to user; if `true`, log warning and try next.
3. Validation at config-set time: reject ambiguous scope patterns (overlapping wildcards), warn about scope `*` not being last.
4. CLI surfaces `resolved from <registry>` on every install for transparency.

**Estimate:** 1-2 hours. Almost entirely CLI logic; no server-side changes.

### Phase M14 — SBOM attestation (§11.14)

**Goal:** Verified packages can attach an SPDX or CycloneDX SBOM at publish time; marketplace surfaces it with vulnerability scanning.

**Status:** Live in production.

**What shipped:**

- Schema `papercusp_marketplace.{package_version_sboms, package_version_vulnerabilities}` + view `v_package_vuln_summary`
- SBOM ingest (`POST /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom`, JSON body): auto-detects SPDX-2.3 vs CycloneDX-1.5, validates JSON, caps at 5 MB, hashes with sha256
- Background scan worker (60s tick): pops `scan_status='pending'`, extracts package URLs from SBOM, batch-queries osv.dev `/v1/querybatch`, persists vulns with severity bucketing
- Endpoints:
  - `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom` — metadata + summary
  - `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` — full vuln list (sorted by severity)
- CLI: `papercusp publish --sbom <path>` flag (uploads after publish, queues scan)
- Marketplace site:
  - `SbomBadge` next to version pill ("✓ No CVEs" green / "⚠ N CVEs" amber/red by worst severity)
  - `SbomSection` at the bottom of detail page (severity chips + collapsible vuln list with deep links to cve.org / github.com/advisories)

**Verified end-to-end:** seeded an SBOM for `signed-test@0.1.0` (lodash@4.17.20 + minimist@1.2.5 components) → osv.dev returned 6 GHSAs (5 lodash + 1 minimist) → all persisted, summary aggregated, exposed at https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/packages/signed-test/0.1.0/sbom + /vulnerabilities.

### What landed this round (M3 + M10 + M13)

**M3 — Tarball signing (Ed25519)**
- Server: keypair auto-generated at startup at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-keys/marketplace-ed25519.{pem,pub}`. New endpoint `GET /v1/keys/marketplace.pub`. Every published tarball gets a `signature.json` sibling file with sha256, signature, and the public key for offline verification. Signed message canonical form: `${slug}\n${version}\n${sha256}\n${publishedBy}\n${publishedAt}\n`.
- Client: `papercusp install` fetches the public key (24h cache at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-keys-cache.json`), recomputes sha256 of the downloaded tarball, and calls `crypto.verify` against the signature. Tampering hard-fails with cleanup of the partial install. Legacy packages without `signature.json` warn but proceed (backward compat). `--no-verify` flag bypasses for offline / debug paths.
- Verified: tampering test (corrupt + retry) correctly rejects with sha256 mismatch error.

**M10 — Size & bandwidth quotas**
- Tarball cap 50 MB (HTTP 413 with clear message), manifest cap 64 KB, README cap 256 KB — all checked at upload before disk write.
- Per-IP rate limit middleware: 600 req/min for read endpoints, 60 tarballs/hour for `/download/`, 5 publishes/min per authenticated publisher (per-IP for unauthenticated). Returns HTTP 429 with `Retry-After` header.
- Per-publisher daily quota tracking at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-storage/.publisher-quotas.json`: 50 publishes/day, 1 GB aggregate storage. Resets at UTC rollover. Only enforces when authenticated.
- Verified: 70 KB manifest correctly rejected; 605 rapid requests yielded 596 × 200 + 9 × 429.

**M13 — Multi-registry resolution**
- CLI reads `~/.papercusp/config.json` for `registries[]` array.
- `resolveRegistry(slug)` walks scopes in order; first match wins. `*` matches anything; `@owner/*` matches `@owner/anything`.
- `--registry <url>` flag overrides config for one-off installs.
- No automatic fallback — if no registry covers the slug, errors with explicit message listing configured scopes.
- Slug regex extended to accept scoped names (`@owner/package`); version splitter handles `@owner/foo@1.2.0` correctly.
- Verified: 4 scenarios — scoped → internal, no-match → error, `--registry` override → bypasses config, no config → falls back to `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_URL`.

Files touched this round:
- `libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-api/src/server.ts` — keypair gen, signing, public key endpoint, rate limit middleware, manifest/README size caps, publisher quota tracking
- `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts` — signature verification on install, `--no-verify` and `--registry` flags, scoped-slug support, registry resolver

Production state after this round:
- `https://api.papercuspai.com/v1/keys/marketplace.pub` — returns Ed25519 public key
- `https://api.papercuspai.com/catalog/signed-test/0.1.0` — includes `signature` field in the response
- Existing legacy packages (papercup-coding, papercup-org) continue to work without signatures

**Original estimate**: 42-52 hours total. **After three rounds shipped (M2.5 + M3 + M4 + M5 + M6 + M7 + M9 + M10 + M13)**: ~17-22 hours remaining. **Remaining work**: M1 (auth — needs your OAuth app), M2 (R2 backing), M8 (authors+reviews), M11 (webhooks), M12 (vendored install), M14 (SBOMs).

### Suggested phase ordering

Not all phases are equal priority. Here's the order I'd run them in, by what unblocks the most usage:

1. **M1 (auth)** — block until landed; everything downstream assumes verified identities.
2. **M2 + M2.5 (R2 + Postgres metadata)** — durability + scale; necessary before significant publishing.
3. **M3 (tarball signing)** — supply chain integrity; prerequisite for verified-tier display.
4. **M7 (detail page UX)** — surface what M1+M3 enable to users.
5. **M5 (update/uninstall)** — close the install loop; users need this before they install anything important.
6. **M10 (quotas)** — anti-abuse before the marketplace is opened publicly.
7. **M6 (retraction)** — operational maturity; needed before a real security incident.
8. **M11 (webhooks)** — unlocks ecosystem integrations.
9. **M4 (search)** — only needed once catalog > ~100 packages.
10. **M9 (stats)** — nice-to-have signal; not blocking.
11. **M8 (reviews)** — community feature; needs moderation tooling.
12. **M12 (vendored)** — enterprise / air-gapped customers.
13. **M13 (multi-registry)** — corporate mirrors with public fallback.
14. **M14 (SBOMs)** — supply chain compliance; v2.0-shaped feature.

## Operational notes

### First-party seed templates (re-publishing)

The bundled templates `papercup-coding` and `papercup-org` are **first-party** —
they're owned by `@papercupai`, not by whoever happens to run the seed script.

Their canonical source-of-truth lives in the marketplace repo at
`../papercusp-registry/seeds/papercupai/<slug>/`. They're published via the
**same publish pipeline as any user package** — no SQL backfill, no special
case in the server.

Two auth modes cover this:

**Service token (recommended for CI / seed scripts):**
A static bearer token bound to a publisher login. The marketplace operator
issues it via `PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_SERVICE_TOKENS` env (JSON array of
`{token, login}` entries). Then:

```bash
PAPERCUSP_SERVICE_TOKEN=<your-token> \
PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_URL=http://localhost:3057 \
  papercusp publish     # from inside seeds/papercupai/<slug>/
```

The CLI sends the token as `Authorization: Bearer ...`; the server matches
it against the configured table and stamps `publishedBy` from the bound login.
No OAuth round-trip, no browser, fully scriptable.

**OAuth Device Flow (for human publishing as @papercupai):**
`papercusp login` then `papercusp publish`. Requires the @papercupai GitHub
account/org to exist and you to be able to authenticate as it.

**Don't** insert seed packages directly via SQL or backfill scripts — that
bypasses the publish pipeline (signing, indexing, webhook events) and creates
orphan-attribution problems. The seeds README at
`../papercusp-registry/seeds/README.md` documents the policy.

### Local development

The marketplace-api runs as a systemd --user transient unit named
`marketplace-api`, defined at `~/.config/systemd/user/marketplace-api.service`.
It's started automatically alongside `bin/dev` and survives shell exits.

```bash
# Status / restart / logs
systemctl --user status marketplace-api
systemctl --user restart marketplace-api
journalctl --user -u marketplace-api -f
# or: tail -f ~/.papercusp/logs/marketplace-api.log

# Manual run (if you need to iterate without the unit):
cd ../papercusp-registry && npm run dev:api      # listens on :3057

# Build + serve site locally
cd ../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site
BUILD_API_BASE=http://localhost:3057 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=https://api.papercuspai.com npm run build
npx serve out -l 3060        # http://localhost:3060
```

### Production deploy

```bash
cd libs/papercusp/apps/marketplace-site
BUILD_API_BASE=http://localhost:3057 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE=https://api.papercuspai.com npm run build
npx wrangler pages deploy ./out --project-name papercuspai --branch main --commit-dirty=true
```

The marketplace-api process must be running on `localhost:3057` for the build's `generateStaticParams` step (which fetches the catalog to pre-render `/marketplace/[slug]/` pages). After M2 lands, this becomes optional — Postgres metadata can serve build-time too.

### Cloudflare touchpoints

- **Pages project:** `papercuspai` (domain attached, deploys via wrangler)
- **Tunnel:** `papercupai-api` (UUID `c53515b3-edfe-4e99-813b-e3916ae9d02c`) — same tunnel as papercupai.com, with two ingress rules (one per hostname)
- **DNS apex:** `papercuspai.com` → `papercuspai.pages.dev` (CNAME, proxied)
- **DNS api:** `api.papercuspai.com` → tunnel UUID via Zero Trust dashboard

### Known operational gotchas

- New publishes appear instantly in `/marketplace/` grid (live API fetch) but **404 on `[slug]` detail until site is rebuilt + redeployed** (`dynamicParams = false` on the static export). Future option: add an SSR fallback at the edge for unknown slugs.
- The CF token at `~/.cloudflare-token` has Pages and a few zone scopes but **NOT** `Account · Cloudflare Tunnel · Edit`. Tunnel changes require dashboard clicks today.
- `cloudflared` runs in token mode → ingress rules managed via Zero Trust dashboard, not `~/.cloudflared/config.yml`.
- Marketplace dirs were moved on 2026-04-27 from `libs/papercusp/apps/{marketplace-api,marketplace-site}` → `../papercusp-registry/apps/{marketplace-api,marketplace-site}`. If you see stale paths anywhere, that's why.
- The `papercusp` CLI (`libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts`) lives in the **substrate** repo, not the marketplace repo. It talks to the marketplace via HTTP, so the split makes sense — but if you change the api shape on the server side, update the CLI in lockstep across both repos.

## Handoff — detailed implementation specs for remaining phases

This section is the precise roadmap for the **3 remaining phases** if a future agent picks up. Each phase has been spec'd in §11 and partially designed earlier; here's what an implementer needs to actually ship them.

### M2 — R2 storage backing (3-4h, **blocked on CF token scope**)

**Why it's blocked:** Need a CF API token with `Account · R2 · Edit` to create the bucket and obtain S3-compatible credentials. The current `~/.cloudflare-token` has Pages + selected zone scopes only.

**Plan once unblocked:**

1. Create R2 bucket `papercusp-marketplace-tarballs` (CF dashboard or API):
   ```
   curl -X POST "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94/r2/buckets" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_R2_TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"name":"papercusp-marketplace-tarballs"}'
   ```

2. Get S3-compatible access keys (CF dashboard → R2 → Manage R2 API Tokens). Add to `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env`:
   ```
   R2_ACCOUNT_ID=f896982ea2f6d507e4f29eeecbd26e94
   R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
   R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
   R2_BUCKET=papercusp-marketplace-tarballs
   ```

3. Add `@aws-sdk/client-s3` to `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/package.json`:
   ```json
   "dependencies": {
     "@aws-sdk/client-s3": "^3.700.0",
     "@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner": "^3.700.0"
   }
   ```

4. Create `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/r2.ts`:
   - `S3Client` configured with `endpoint: https://${R2_ACCOUNT_ID}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, `region: 'auto'`
   - `uploadTarball(slug, version, buf)` → `s3.send(new PutObjectCommand(...))`
   - `getDownloadUrl(slug, version)` → `getSignedUrl(s3, new GetObjectCommand(...), { expiresIn: 300 })`
   - Key format: `tarballs/${slug}/${version}/${slug}-${version}.tar.gz`

5. Modify `server.ts` publish handler:
   - After existing FS write to `tarballPath`, also call `uploadTarball(slug, version, buf)`
   - Continue dual-writing FS for now (rollback safety)

6. Modify `server.ts` `/download/:slug/:version`:
   - First try the R2 signed URL: redirect 302 to it
   - On any error (R2 down or migration not complete), fall back to existing FS stream
   - `papercusp_marketplace.package_versions.tarball_r2_key` column tracks if uploaded — add a migration

7. Migration script: `../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/migrate-to-r2.ts` — iterates existing FS packages, uploads each to R2, marks `tarball_r2_key` in the DB.

8. Delete FS storage AFTER verifying R2 + signed URLs serve correctly for a week.

**Schema delta (002b):**
```sql
ALTER TABLE papercusp_marketplace.package_versions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS tarball_r2_key TEXT;
```

**Testing:**
- Unit: upload + signed URL roundtrip
- Integration: publish via CLI, verify install pulls from R2 (302 redirect chain visible)
- Failure mode: simulate R2 outage with bad credentials, verify FS fallback engages

### M8 — Author profiles + reviews (4-5h)

**Schema** (003b-reviews.sql in `../papercusp-registry/sql/`):
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS papercusp_marketplace.reviews (
  id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                  -- 'rv_' + 24 hex
  slug          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES papercusp_marketplace.packages(slug) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  reviewer      TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- verified GitHub login
  rating        SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5),
  body          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 10 AND 5000),
  created_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  hidden_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,                       -- non-null = operator hid
  hidden_reason TEXT,
  UNIQUE (slug, reviewer)                          -- one review per user per package
);

CREATE INDEX reviews_slug_idx ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews(slug);
CREATE INDEX reviews_reviewer_idx ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews(reviewer);

GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON papercusp_marketplace.reviews TO harness_app, harness_admin;
```

**Endpoints in `server.ts`:**
- `GET /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — list reviews (excludes hidden_at IS NOT NULL); 50 most recent
- `POST /v1/packages/:slug/reviews` — auth-required, insert/update by `(slug, reviewer)`. Reject if reviewer is the package's `publishedBy` (no self-reviews). Reject if account < 7 days old (anti-spam).
- `DELETE /v1/packages/:slug/reviews/:id` — owner of the review only
- `POST /v1/admin/reviews/:id/hide` — operator-only; sets `hidden_at` + `hidden_reason`
- `GET /v1/authors/:login` — public profile + their packages + their reviews (last 10)

**Site changes** (`../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-site/`):
- New page `/authors/[login]/page.tsx` with `generateStaticParams` from `package_versions.published_by DISTINCT`
- New section on `/marketplace/[slug]/` (PackageClient.tsx) with reviews list + write-review form (auth-gated)
- Average rating badge on the catalog grid

**Anti-abuse rules** (per spec §8 of M8 plan):
- Reviewers from accounts < 7 days old: visible but flagged "new account"
- Reviews can be reported via `POST /v1/packages/:slug/reviews/:id/report`
- Operator UI later (deferred) for moderation queue

### M14 — SBOM attestation + CVE scanning (6-8h)

**Schema** (005-attestations.sql):
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations (
  slug              TEXT NOT NULL,
  version           TEXT NOT NULL,
  format            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (format IN ('spdx', 'cyclonedx')),
  sbom_json         JSONB NOT NULL,
  scanned_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
  vulnerabilities   JSONB,                         -- [{ purl, advisory_id, severity, fixedIn }]
  PRIMARY KEY (slug, version),
  FOREIGN KEY (slug, version) REFERENCES papercusp_marketplace.package_versions(slug, version) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE INDEX attestations_unscanned_idx
  ON papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations(scanned_at) WHERE scanned_at IS NULL;
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON papercusp_marketplace.package_attestations TO harness_app, harness_admin;
```

**Publish handler change:**
- `POST /publish/:slug/:version` accepts an additional multipart field `sbom` (JSON file). Validate against the format's JSON schema before storing. If valid, insert into `package_attestations` with `scanned_at = NULL`.

**Scan worker** (`../papercusp-registry/apps/marketplace-api/src/sbom-scanner.ts`):
- Long-lived loop (1-min tick) drains rows where `scanned_at IS NULL`
- For each: extract package list (SPDX `packages[]` or CycloneDX `components[]`)
- For each package: query `https://api.osv.dev/v1/query` with PURL or CPE
- Store findings in `vulnerabilities[]`
- Re-scan all attestations weekly (set `scanned_at = NULL` for rows older than 7d)
- Rate limit: max 10 osv.dev queries/sec; back off on 429

**Endpoints:**
- `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom` — raw SBOM JSON
- `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/sbom/viewer` — formatted HTML (server-side render via marked.js or similar)
- `GET /v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` — current findings

**Site changes:**
- "Has SBOM" badge on detail page (already wired UI: just add a check)
- Vulnerability count badge if `vulnerabilities.length > 0`
- Optional: SBOM diff between two versions (deferred to v2)

**CLI:**
- `papercusp publish --sbom ./sbom.spdx.json` — multipart upload
- `papercusp install` warns if installed plugin has unpatched CVEs (queries `/v1/packages/:slug/:version/vulnerabilities` after install)

## Quick-start for a future agent

If you're picking this up cold, here's the 5-minute orientation:

1. **Where the code lives**:
   - Substrate: `Papercusp/papercusp` repo → submodule at `<reference-app>/libs/papercusp/`
   - Marketplace: `Papercusp/papercusp-registry` repo → submodule at `<reference-app>/../papercusp-registry/`
   - Spec docs: embedded in `<reference-app>/apps/papercusp/content/docs/` and served at `localhost:3055/docs` (Fumadocs). Legacy Starlight source still in `<reference-app>/apps/papercusp-spec/`.
   - Substrate UI: `libs/papercusp/apps/web/` (lives at `localhost:3055`)
   - CLI: `libs/papercusp/packages/cli/src/papercusp.ts`

2. **How to start everything**:
   ```bash
   cd ~/reference-app
   # marketplace-api (port 3057):
   bash -c 'set -a; source $HOME/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env; set +a; nohup npm run dev:marketplace > /tmp/marketplace-api.log 2>&1 &'
   # spec docs are now served by apps/papercusp at /docs (no separate process):
   #   already running at http://localhost:3055/docs once papercusp dev is up
   # admin web (port 3001):
   cd apps/web/.next/standalone/apps/web && PORT=3001 HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0 nohup node server.js > /tmp/web-prod.log 2>&1 &
   # substrate web (port 3055):
   cd ~/reference-app && nohup npm run dev:papercusp > /tmp/papercusp-web.log 2>&1 &
   ```

3. **How to verify everything is up**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w ":3057 healthz: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3057/healthz
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w ":3055 substrate UI: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3055/
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w ":3001 admin: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3001/
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w ":3055 docs: %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:3055/docs
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "papercuspai.com: %{http_code}\n" https://papercuspai.com/
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w "api.papercuspai.com: %{http_code}\n" https://api.papercuspai.com/healthz
   ```

4. **The Postgres state**:
   ```sql
   -- in `papercusp` DB, schema `papercusp_marketplace`
   SELECT 'packages' AS t, COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.packages
   UNION ALL SELECT 'package_versions', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.package_versions
   UNION ALL SELECT 'package_downloads', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.package_downloads
   UNION ALL SELECT 'package_retraction_log', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.package_retraction_log
   UNION ALL SELECT 'sessions', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.sessions
   UNION ALL SELECT 'webhook_subscriptions', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.webhook_subscriptions
   UNION ALL SELECT 'webhook_deliveries', COUNT(*) FROM papercusp_marketplace.webhook_deliveries;
   ```

5. **The full env file** at `~/.papercusp/marketplace-secrets.env` (mode 0600):
   ```
   GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID=...
   GITHUB_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET=...
   PAPERCUSP_MARKETPLACE_OPERATOR_TOKEN=...
   PAPERCUSP_SESSION_HMAC_KEY=...
   ```

6. **Submodule SHAs** to know about (for reference):
   - `Papercusp/papercusp` master at `8374a93` (extract marketplace commit)
   - `Papercusp/papercusp-registry` master at `756aaa4` (initial extract commit)
